title: Isomer Insight: cis/trans and Optical
welcome_lead: Map the isomers of complex ions and their structural diversity.
meta_desc: A-Level chemistry adventure on complex ion isomerism.
final_note: You learnt to mirror and rotate complex ions.

walkthroughs.body_html:
For [Pt(NH3)2Cl2]: cis has both NH3 adjacent (90 deg); trans has NH3 opposite (180 deg).

cis-platin binds DNA between adjacent guanines to halt cell division (cancer therapy). Trans isomer inactive.

[Co(NH3)4Cl2]+: two Cl can be cis (90 deg) or trans (180 deg). Cis isomer is purple; trans is green.

cis form often optically active if it lacks a mirror plane.

Three bidentate ligands around an octahedral centre (e.g. [Co(en)3]^3+) make a non-superimposable mirror pair.

Detected by rotation of plane-polarised light (Λ and Δ enantiomers).

mcqs.q: If a complex ion has a coordination number of 4, what shape does it have?
options: A coordination number of 4 always means tetrahedral, because that gives the maximum bond-angle separation.
Transition metals are coloured because their nuclei emit photons in the visible range.
It can be either tetrahedral OR square planar — the shape depends on the metal and ligands (e.g. [Pt(NH3)4]2+ is square planar; [CuCl4]2- is tetrahedral).
A coordination number of 4 always means square planar because complexes prefer to be flat.

mcqs.q: Why are most transition metal complex ions coloured?
options: Transition metal ions are coloured because they have a half-full d-subshell which naturally absorbs light.
Transition metals are coloured because their nuclei emit photons in the visible range.
Ligands split the d-orbitals into two energy levels; electrons absorb visible light to jump between them (d-d transitions), and the complementary colour is transmitted.
A coordination number of 4 always means square planar because complexes prefer to be flat.

mcqs.q: Why can transition metals show variable oxidation states?
options: Transition metals have variable oxidation states because they can gain protons easily.
The 4s and 3d orbitals are similar in energy, so different numbers of electrons can be removed without a large energy cost.
A coordination number of 4 always means square planar because complexes prefer to be flat.
Transition metals have variable oxidation states because they have many shells of electrons.
